cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is cross-run observational memory?
cards.answer: The practice of having an agent system record, for each session, a compressed observation of what it attempted and how it turned out (strategy chosen, attempt number, outcome, tokens spent), and read that accumulated history back on later runs — so a system stateless within a run still improves across runs instead of restarting from zero.

cards.heading: Key mechanism: observations vs. raw transcripts
cards.question: What is the key distinction between hauling raw context forward and cross-run observational memory's approach?
cards.answer: Raw transcripts are large, mostly irrelevant, and grow without bound. An observation is a small structured record — strategy, unit, round, result, cost — that is cheap to store as an append-only event log and cheap to query.

cards.heading: Selective read-back
cards.question: What does the structured format of observations enable that a purely stateless evaluate-keep-or-revert loop cannot do?
cards.answer: Selective read-back: the next run can select on prior records, so a unit that stalled under a particular strategy last time can start higher on its escalation ladder. A stateless loop can run a hundred experiments overnight without knowing which strategies worked last week.

cards.heading: Aggregate trend queries
cards.question: What can aggregate queries over the observational log answer that individual records cannot?
cards.answer: Whether the system is trending toward more fixes for fewer tokens over time.

cards.heading: Hard requirement: harness instrumentation
cards.question: What must be true of an agent harness for cross-run observational memory to work at all?
cards.answer: The harness must emit per-attempt structured telemetry — a system that records nothing between input and output cannot learn between runs by any means.
